reviews.notes: Accurately represents Arjuna's confession that his delusion is dispelled by hearing the supreme secret of Adhyatman.
Directly matches knowing the origin and dissolution of beings and Krishna's inexhaustible greatness; footnote 21 preserved.
Faithfully renders Arjuna longing to see the Sovereign Lord's divine Form as described.
Captures the petition that if it be possible for mortal sight to bear, the Lord of Yoga reveal His imperishable Self.
Accurately renders Krishna bidding Arjuna behold hundreds and thousands of divine, multiform shapes and hues.
Directly enumerates Adityas, Vasus, Rudras, the twin Asvins, Maruts, and unnumbered wonders never seen before.
Faithfully renders beholding the entire universe of moving and unmoving things concentrated in one within Krishna's body.
Matches giving the divine eye (divyaṃ cakṣuḥ) since mortal eyes cannot behold the lordly Yoga.
Accurately represents Sanjaya narrating how Hari, the Great Lord of Yoga, revealed His supreme divine form.
Faithfully renders the myriad eyes, mouths, wonderful visions, celestial ornaments, and upraised heavenly weapons.
Matches divine garlands, lustrous robes, celestial perfumes, and all-facing infinite magnificence.
Accurately captures the famous simile comparing the cosmic effulgence to a thousand suns blazing forth simultaneously in the sky.
Directly matches Pandava seeing the manifold diversity of the universe united in the one body of the God of gods.
Captures Arjuna filled with wonder, hairs standing on end, bowing with joined palms in adoration.
Accurately renders Arjuna seeing all the devas, diverse living beings, Brahma on His lotus-seat, rishis, and divine serpents.
Faithfully renders the countless arms, bellies, faces, and eyes on every side, seeing no beginning, middle, or end.
Directly matches the crown (anadem/diadem), mace/club, discus, and blinding radiance blazing like fire and sun.
Corresponds to the supreme Imperishable, treasure-house of the cosmos, guardian of eternal dharma, and everlasting Purusha.
Accurately renders without beginning/middle/end, sun and moon as eyes, blazing fire as mouth, and warming the universe with splendour.
Matches pervading space between heaven and earth and all directions, causing the three worlds to tremble before this terrible form.
Faithfully renders hosts of gods entering in awe with joined palms, and rishis and siddhas chanting 'Hail' in glorious hymns.
Accurately lists Rudras, Adityas, Vasus, Sadhyas, Viswas, Ushmapas, Maruts, Asvins, Gandharvas, and Asuras gazing in fear; footnote 22 preserved.
Directly matches the stupendous form with myriad mouths, eyes, arms, thighs, bellies, and frightful tusks shaking the worlds and Arjuna.
Captures the form touching heaven, blazing with many hues, open mouths, and huge fiery eyes shattering Arjuna's strength and peace.
Accurately represents mouths terrible with teeth resembling dissolution fires (kālānala), losing sense of direction, begging mercy.
Shared two-verse span with 11.27 verified; Arnold interweaves the enumerated warriors (Dhritarashtra's sons, Bhishma, Drona, Karna) with their destruction in the jaws.
Shared two-verse span with 11.26 verified; correctly captures warriors caught between the teeth and ground into dust in the wide gorge.
Accurately preserves the simile of rivers rushing headlong into the sea, matching the heroes rushing into the flaming mouths.
Preserves the simile of moths fluttering toward flame to their doom, matching multitudes rushing blindly to their destruction.
Directly renders licking and devouring all worlds on every side with flaming jaws and filling the earth with burning dread.
Captures Arjuna imploring who this fierce deity is, offering salutations with Namostu Te, Devavara! Prasid! [FN#23].
Faithfully renders Krishna declaring Himself as all-destroying Time (kālo'smi), doomed warriors doomed to fall even without Arjuna.
Accurately represents the call to arise, win fame, and conquer, being merely an instrument (nimittamātraṃ bhava) for what is already ordained.
Directly names Drona, Bhishma, Jayadratha, and Karna as already slain by the Lord, commanding Arjuna to fight without distress.
Matches Sanjaya describing Arjuna trembling, clasping lifted palms, prostrating, and speaking in choked, fearful accents.
Accurately reflects the world delighting in Krishna's glory, rakshasas fleeing in fear to all quarters, and siddhas bowing.
Matches acknowledging the Lord as greater than Brahma, first Creator, infinite God of gods, being and non-being.
Faithfully renders the Primal God, ancient Purusha, supreme treasure-refuge, Knower, Knowable, and pervasive Infinite Form.
Accurately maps Vayu [FN#24], Yama, Agni, Varuna, Moon, Prajapati, Great-grandfather, offering thousandfold salutations.
Directly renders salutations before, behind, and on all sides, acknowledging infinite prowess pervadeth all.
Captures Arjuna's apology for addressing Krishna familiarly as friend, Yadava, or comrade through carelessness or affection.
Matches seeking forgiveness for any discourtesy shown in jest, while resting, sitting, eating, alone, or in company.
Directly corresponds to Father of all worlds moving and unmoving, greatest Guru, unequalled and peerless in power.
Faithfully renders prostrating and begging grace as father to son, friend to friend, and lover to beloved.
Captures rejoicing at seeing the unseen yet shaken by dread, pleading for the previous familiar divine form to be shown.
Directly matches desiring to behold the crown, mace, and discus in hand, assuming once more the four-armed charioteer guise.
Accurately represents Krishna stating this supreme, luminous, cosmic form was graciously revealed through His own Yoga to Arjuna alone.
Matches that neither Vedic study, sacrifices, alms, rituals, nor severe penances enable any mortal to see this form.
Faithfully renders Krishna bidding Arjuna put aside fear and bewilderment, looking once more upon His accustomed form.
Matches Sanjaya recounting Vasudeva reassuming His gentle human form to comfort the terrified prince.
Accurately represents Arjuna regaining calm and returning to his natural composure upon seeing Krishna's friendly human guise.
Captures the declaration that this form is very hard to see, continually desired and sought even by the gods.
Reiterates that neither Vedas, penance, gifts, nor sacrifices can grant vision of this form as witnessed by Arjuna.
Directly matches that only by single-minded devotion (bhaktyā tvananyayā) can the Lord be truly known, seen, and entered into.
Accurately renders the essential closing verse: he who works for Krishna, devoted, free from attachment and malice toward all, reaches Him.

chapterFindings: Chapter 11 contains 55 canonical verses; verses 11.26 and 11.27 form a verified shared two-verse span where Arnold combines the naming of the warriors with their horrifying destruction in the cosmic jaws.
The chapter transitions across multiple lyric metrical forms (including rhymed stanzas for Sanjaya's description and Arjuna's awe-filled hymn) without losing semantic fidelity or verse boundaries.
Footnotes [FN#21], [FN#22], [FN#23], and [FN#24] are properly preserved and positioned.
